name: Kitten Vaccination Checklist
description: A checklist to help new kitten owners follow the typical vaccine series, track each shot, and stay on schedule with their veterinarian.

items.text: Confirm your kitten's age and any shelter records
Gather paperwork on shots already given
Note your kitten's weight and overall health
Write down questions about diet, parasites, and litter habits
Book the first vet visit soon after bringing kitten home
items.note: Ask your vet to set the right start date for your kitten

items.text: First combination vaccine for feline viruses as advised
General health and weight check with your vet
Discuss a deworming and parasite plan
Ask about a feline leukemia test and prevention
Record the date and set the next appointment
items.note: Timing varies by region and vet, so confirm your kitten's schedule

items.text: Second combination booster as recommended
Feline leukemia vaccine if outdoor access is likely
Continue the deworming or parasite plan
Review socialization, handling, and litter training
Log the visit and confirm the next due date
Final combination booster of the kitten series
Rabies vaccine where required by law or your vet
Confirm when adult boosters will next be due
Discuss spay or neuter timing if relevant
Ask when outdoor access is safe if planned
items.note: Vets differ on exact timing, so follow your vet's guidance

items.text: Watch for mild soreness, tiredness, or low appetite
Note any swelling, vomiting, or distress to report
Give your kitten a calm, quiet place to rest
Update the record and set the next reminder
Keep a copy ready for boarding or travel
items.note: Contact your vet promptly if you see a strong reaction

items.text: Keep a running log of each vaccine and date
Save batch numbers and the clinic that gave each shot
Register and confirm your kitten's microchip details
Plan the first adult booster visit
Store a digital backup of the full kitten record
This checklist is general information for owners, not veterinary advice; kitten vaccine schedules vary by region and vet, so always consult a licensed veterinarian
items.note: For any reaction or emergency, contact your vet or an emergency animal hospital immediately

faq.q: When do kitten vaccinations usually start?
faq.a: Kitten shots often begin around six to eight weeks of age and continue in a series every few weeks. The exact start depends on your kitten's age and health, so confirm timing with your veterinarian.

faq.q: How many rounds of shots does a kitten need?
faq.a: Most kittens receive several rounds spaced a few weeks apart, typically finishing around sixteen weeks or later. The number of doses varies by vaccine and protocol, so follow your vet's plan.

faq.q: Do indoor kittens need vaccines too?
faq.a: Often yes. Some vaccines are recommended even for indoor cats, while others depend on outdoor access and exposure. Your veterinarian will advise which vaccines your kitten needs.

faq.q: What if we miss a kitten vaccine appointment?
faq.a: Contact your veterinarian as soon as possible. They will advise whether to continue where you left off or repeat part of the series so your kitten stays protected.

faq.q: Is this kitten vaccination checklist printable?
faq.a: Yes. Print it or download the PDF, record each shot and date by week, and bring it to appointments to keep your kitten's series on track.
